Sitemap

A simple directory of the main pages and sections across Aaron Schlossberg’s Universe.

Exploring the Universe

Aaron Schlossberg’s Universe brings together my projects, writing, education, interests, collections, and creative explorations. Some pages introduce broad areas of my work, while others lead into individual stories, resources, experiences, and ideas.

There are several ways to navigate this growing website. Main Pages provides quick access to its central destinations. Browse by Section organizes related pages beneath their parent sections, including larger collections that can expand over time. All Pages offers a single directory with a short explanation of each destination.

Pages are arranged according to where they belong in the site, not necessarily when they were created. As new content is published, these directories can grow alongside it. For the full range of material within a particular collection, you can also visit its dedicated index page.

  15. ├─┤Just This Once: Read “Just This Once”, a speculative-horror short story by Aaron L. Schlossberg about envy, temptation, and a mysterious stone.
  16. ├─┤R.I.P. (Rest in Progress): Rita and Ace visit a graveyard after dark and find headstones with dates that leave too much unsaid. R.I.P. (Rest in Progress) is a short story by Aaron L. Schlossberg.
  17. ├─┤1080 Rewires: A repair order sends 1080 and Sal into a maze of yellow corridors where the route back won’t stay put. 1080 Rewires is a short story by Aaron L. Schlossberg.
  18. ├─┤Elegant Eats: Two figures in hyena masks storm a restaurant, bringing Cynthia face-to-face with a promise made ten years ago. Elegant Eats is a short story by Aaron L. Schlossberg.
  19. ├─┤Autumn: The fall of a single leaf looks different to the leaf, the squirrel beneath it, and the forest around them. Autumn is a short story by Aaron L. Schlossberg.
  20. ├─┤The Equation of Quiet: A figure in Lucas’s dreams tells him he owes the world a share of his voice, then leaves him to work out how much. The Equation of Quiet is a short story by Aaron L. Schlossberg.
  21. ├─┤No One Else Was in The Dream Where it Happened: Juniper starts keeping notes on his dreams when their doors, mirrors, and familiar faces begin to cross over. No One Else Was in The Dream Where it Happened is a flash fiction by Aaron L. Schlossberg.
  22. ├─┤Where I’m From: A fictional speaker traces where they come from through small objects, remembered sounds, and the things they almost said. Where I’m From is a persona poem by Aaron L. Schlossberg.

  29. /Compendium: A searchable glossary of terms and ideas that come up across the site.
  30. ├─┤Anemoia: Nostalgia for a time you never lived through.
  31. ├─┤The Astley Paradox: An internet joke about asking Rick Astley for the film Up and treating either possible answer as a broken promise from his best-known song.
  32. ├─┤The Backrooms: A fictional maze of seemingly endless rooms and corridors, often entered by slipping out of ordinary reality.
  33. ├─┤Boots Theory: Sam Vimes’s idea that people with less money upfront can end up paying more over time because they can only afford goods that need frequent replacement.
  34. ├─┤Byway: A smaller or less-traveled road, often away from a main route.
  35. ├─┤Cognitive Bias: A systematic tendency in thinking or judgment that can affect how people interpret information and make decisions.
  36. ├─┤Cognitive Dissonance: Psychological discomfort associated with holding conflicting beliefs or with acting in a way that conflicts with one’s beliefs.
  37. ├─┤Cognitive Economy: The use of mental categories or shortcuts to gain useful information while conserving limited attention and effort.
  38. ├─┤Collective Unconscious: Carl Jung’s proposed shared layer of the unconscious, containing inherited patterns he called archetypes.
  39. ├─┤Compendium: A concise collection of information about a subject or a range of subjects.
  40. ├─┤Creepypasta: A horror story that spreads online through copying, reposting, or retelling.
  41. ├─┤CSS: Cascading Style Sheets, the language used to control the presentation and layout of web content.
  42. ├─┤Deltarune: A role-playing game by Toby Fox that follows a group of characters through mysterious worlds, combining exploration, dialogue, and patterned battles.
  43. ├─┤Disney: The entertainment company and brand associated with animation, films, characters, and themed destinations such as Disneyland and Walt Disney World.
  44. ├─┤Disney World: Walt Disney World Resort, the Disney resort near Orlando, Florida, with four theme parks and a wider collection of hotels and experiences.
  45. ├─┤Disneyland (California): Disney’s original theme park in Anaheim, California, which opened in 1955.
  46. ├─┤Emoji: A pictorial symbol used in digital text to express an idea, object, reaction, or emotion.
  47. ├─┤Emoticon: An expression made from text characters, such as :-) or :-(, to suggest a face or convey a feeling.
  48. ├─┤Enshittification: Cory Doctorow’s term for the deterioration of a platform as its operators shift benefits away from users and partners toward extracting more value for themselves.
  49. ├─┤Expository Writing: Writing that explains, informs, or clarifies a subject through organized information and examples.
  50. ├─┤Felix Felicis: The luck-enhancing potion in Harry Potter, also known as Liquid Luck.
  51. ├─┤Forlornness: A feeling or appearance of loneliness, abandonment, or hopeless sadness.
  52. ├─┤Found Footage: A storytelling technique that presents a film as recordings recovered from within the story.
  53. ├─┤The Game: A mind game whose goal is to avoid thinking about the Game. Thinking about it counts as a loss, which players commonly announce.
  54. ├─┤Gift Economy: A system in which goods or services circulate through giving and social relationships, often with expectations of reciprocity.
  55. ├─┤Gordian Knot: An exceptionally difficult or tangled problem, named for the ancient story of Alexander the Great and an intricate knot.
  56. ├─┤Halloweekend: An informal name for a weekend of Halloween celebrations.
  57. ├─┤HTML: HyperText Markup Language, the language used to give web content its structure and meaning.
  58. ├─┤JavaScript: A programming language widely used to add behavior and interactivity to websites.
  59. ├─┤Kane Parsons: A filmmaker and visual-effects artist, known online as Kane Pixels, whose Backrooms videos turn familiar spaces into unsettling fictional environments.
  60. ├─┤Kenopsia: The eerie feeling of being somewhere that’s usually busy when everyone is gone.
  61. ├─┤Level 0: The familiar yellow-room setting that serves as the first area in many versions of the Backrooms. It is often called “The Lobby”.
  62. ├─┤Liminal Space: A place or state in between. In online photography and art, it often means a familiar place that feels strangely removed from its usual purpose.
  63. ├─┤Luminary: A person distinguished for their influence or achievements in a field. The word can also mean a source of light.
  64. ├─┤Marvin’s Friend: The Lifeform encountered by Marvin Leigh in Kane Pixels’s Backrooms - Pitfalls, later jokingly called “Marvin’s Friend” in the series.
  65. ├─┤Metanostalgia: Nostalgia for nostalgia itself, or longing for the way an experience once made you feel.
  66. ├─┤Multipotentialite: Someone who pursues several interests or creative paths, sometimes bringing them together in the same work.
  67. ├─┤Noclip: To pass through walls or floors that would normally block a player in a game. In Backrooms stories, it means slipping out of ordinary reality.
  68. ├─┤Nostalgia: A wistful, often bittersweet longing for the past.
  69. ├─┤Numinous: Evoking a sense of sacred or mysterious presence, often with awe.
  70. ├─┤OP (Original Poster): The person who started an online post or discussion thread.
  71. ├─┤OP (Overpowered): A description of a character, ability, item, or strategy whose power is unusually high compared with the challenge or its alternatives.
  72. ├─┤Philanthropy: Efforts to promote other people’s well-being or the public good, often through giving money, time, expertise, or other resources.
  73. ├─┤Pokédex: An encyclopedia within Pokémon games that records information about the Pokémon a Trainer encounters or catches.
  74. ├─┤Pokémon: A franchise about discovering, befriending, training, and battling creatures called Pokémon, spanning video games, cards, animation, and more.
  75. ├─┤Question-and-Answer Site: A website organized around people asking questions and receiving answers from other users.
  76. ├─┤Reality Distortion Field: A phrase associated with Steve Jobs for persuasive confidence that can reshape how other people judge what is possible.
  77. ├─┤SB-129: A SpongeBob SquarePants episode in which Squidward’s attempts to find peace take him through time and into a strangely empty space.
  78. ├─┤Sectumsempra: A harmful spell in Harry Potter that causes severe cuts to its target.
  79. ├─┤Specious: Superficially plausible, but actually wrong.
  80. ├─┤Spoonerism: A mix-up in which the opening sounds of two words exchange places, often producing a humorous phrase.
  81. ├─┤Static Front-End Website: A website whose pages are delivered as prepared files, with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and other assets handling what visitors see and use.
  82. ├─┤Technical Writing: Writing that helps a particular audience understand a technical subject or complete a technical task.
  83. ├─┤Toby Fox: A game creator and composer best known for Undertale and Deltarune.
  84. ├─┤Torii: A traditional Japanese gate that marks an entrance or boundary associated with a Shinto shrine.
  85. ├─┤Undertale: A role-playing game by Toby Fox in which a human explores an underground world of monsters, with choices about fighting and showing mercy.
  86. ├─┤Worldbuilding: Creating a fictional setting and the details that make it feel like a place of its own, such as its geography, history, culture, or rules.
  87. ├─┤XP/EXP: Common abbreviations for experience points, a game resource used to measure progress and often advance a character’s level or abilities.
  88. /Favorite Quotes: A searchable and filterable collection of quotations that have stayed with me.
  89. /Sitemap: Browse a human-friendly map of Aaron Schlossberg’s Universe, organized by projects, writings, education, images, personal information, and utilities.
